title: TSMC affiliate already eyes expansion as first Singapore plant 'sells out'
gist: Vanguard International Semiconductor's Singapore JV with NXP (VSMC) opened its first 300mm fab with planned capacity already reserved by customers on AI-linked demand, and VIS is weighing a second Singapore plant; volume production starts 1Q27, reaching ~44k wafers/month by 2029.

insights.claim: Vanguard International Semiconductor, a TSMC affiliate, inaugurated its Tampines, Singapore fab on September 28 through its joint venture with NXP and is considering a second Singapore plant because customers have claimed the first plant's planned capacity.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Pre-sold mature-node/specialty capacity suggests tighter supply in power, analog and interposer segments.

insights.claim: 'Sold out' at the VSMC fab refers to production capacity committed to customers rather than chips already made; the plant still must ramp, with commercial volume production scheduled for Q1 2027.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Execution risk on the ramp remains even with reserved demand.
insights.quote: The phrase “sold out” refers to production capacity committed to customers, not chips already made.

insights.claim: The VSMC fab is expected to reach about 44,000 12-inch wafers per month by 2029 and create roughly 1,600 jobs when fully built out.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Sizes new 300mm specialty capacity entering the market through 2029.

insights.claim: The VSMC joint venture completed construction in under two years and says its first sample batch achieved yields above 99%.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Fast build and high early yields de-risk the ramp schedule.

insights.claim: NXP said its planned manufacturing capacity at the VSMC joint venture has not changed, while Vanguard has discussed accelerating a second phase.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Incremental capacity upside accrues to Vanguard rather than NXP.

insights.claim: The VSMC fab will make power management, analog and mixed-signal chips plus interposers for chip packaging, and AI infrastructure demand has helped fill its planned output.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: AI demand is spilling over into mature-node power/analog and interposer capacity, not just leading-edge logic.
insights.quote: Demand tied to AI infrastructure has helped fill the plant’s planned output

insights.claim: The Singapore plant gives Vanguard a larger manufacturing foothold outside Taiwan as chipmakers respond to customer demand for geographically diverse supply.
insights.speaker: B
insights.so_what: Supply-chain diversification away from Taiwan continues to drive capex in Southeast Asia.
